legislative_history.event: EU transposition deadline passed without enactment
European Commission sends reasoned opinion to Portugal
Authorization Law 59/2025 published, granting government 180 days to enact implementing legislation
Decreto-Lei 125/2025 published in Diario da Republica
Entry into force (120 days after publication)

competent_authority.name: Centro Nacional de Ciberseguranca
competent_authority.role: National cybersecurity authority, CSIRT, entity classification, supervision, registration platform operator
competent_authority.supervisory_body: Gabinete Nacional de Seguranca (GNS), under the Prime Minister's office

essential_entities.description: Entities in Annex I sectors exceeding medium-sized enterprise thresholds (250+ employees OR EUR 50M+ turnover OR EUR 43M+ balance sheet), plus qualified trust service providers, domain registries, medium-sized telecom companies, critical public administration entities
essential_entities.size_threshold: 250+ employees OR EUR 50M+ turnover OR EUR 43M+ balance sheet

important_entities.description: Non-essential entities from Annex I/II sectors meeting medium-sized enterprise thresholds

incident_reporting.initial_notification: 24 hours from identifying a significant incident
incident_reporting.authority_response: CNCS responds to initial notification within 24 hours

essential_entities.maximum: EUR 10,000,000 or 2% of annual global turnover, whichever is higher

important_entities.maximum: EUR 7,000,000 or 1.4% of annual global turnover, whichever is higher

penalties.additional: Ancillary sanctions and compulsory financial penalties for non-compliance

compliance_deadlines.cybersecurity_officer_appointment: 2026-05-04 (20 working days from entry into force, Art. 31)
compliance_deadlines.entity_registration: 60 days from CNCS platform availability for existing entities; 30 days from activity commencement for new entities (Art. 8, 35)
compliance_deadlines.risk_management_measures: 24 months from CNCS supplementary regulations issuance (Art. 27)
compliance_deadlines.supply_chain_measures: 24 months from CNCS supplementary regulations issuance (Art. 28)
compliance_deadlines.annual_reports: 24 months from CNCS supplementary regulations issuance (Art. 30)

management_liability.description: Board members face liability for intentional actions or gross negligence in cybersecurity infringements. Management must approve risk management measures, supervise implementation, and ensure regularity of cybersecurity training (Art. 25). Responsibility cannot be fully delegated except to individual board members.

supply_chain_requirements.description: Measures must address supplier vulnerabilities, product cybersecurity quality, supplier practices, coordinated risk assessments, and decisions regarding ICT equipment restrictions (Art. 28)

cybersecurity_officer.requirement: Must be a member of the entity's management bodies or directly subordinate to them
cybersecurity_officer.responsibilities: Propose cybersecurity measures, inform leadership of risks, manage residual risk, coordinate incident response

key_articles.Art. 25: Management body responsibilities: approve measures, supervise implementation, ensure training
key_articles.Art. 29: Residual risk management and business continuity

infringement_proceedings.status: Reasoned opinion sent; subsequently transposed in December 2025

sources.title: Morais Leitao - Legal Alert: New legal framework for cybersecurity
VdA - NIS 2 Directive transposed in Portugal
iCompliance - NIS2 implementation in Portugal: practical roadmap

notes: CNCS is the competent authority for all NIS2 obligations
Law enters into force on 2026-04-03 — 8 days away as of last verification
24-hour incident notification mandatory for significant incidents; unique end-of-impact notification also within 24h
Covers public administration entities beyond base NIS2 scope (Relevant Public Entities Groups A and B)
Cybersecurity officer must be board member or directly subordinate — appointment deadline May 4, 2026
Management training is mandatory under Art. 25 (regularity of cybersecurity training actions)
Key technical/organizational measures (Art. 27-30) have 24-month delayed enforcement pending CNCS supplementary regulations
Law represents a profound reformulation of the Portuguese cybersecurity legal framework, replacing Law 46/2018
Crisis Office composed of entities responsible for internal security, defense, and criminal investigation
Important entities: lower penalty cap (EUR 7M / 1.4%) vs essential entities (EUR 10M / 2%)
